subtitle: Lesson 39 · Building a Transformer From Scratch

code:
x = x + sublayer(x)

# the "+" gives gradients a direct
# identity path backward through
# every block -- no matter how deep

# same motivation as an LSTM's
# additive cell-state path
caption: Without the residual add, deep stacks suffer vanishing gradients.

code:
norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)

# per token, over the d_model axis:
# (x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps)
#   * weight + bias

# mean/var computed PER TOKEN,
# not across batch or sequence
caption: Every token's own features get rescaled to ~zero mean, unit variance.

steps.label: Post-norm (2017 paper)
steps.sub: x = norm(x + sublayer(x)) -- normalize AFTER the add

steps.label: Pre-norm (modern default)
steps.sub: x = x + sublayer(norm(x)) -- normalize BEFORE the sublayer

steps.label: Post-norm
steps.sub: residual path gets rescaled every block -- never fully clean

steps.label: Pre-norm
steps.sub: x on the left of + is never touched -- stays clean end to end

steps.label: Trade-off
steps.sub: post-norm: slightly better small-scale results; pre-norm: trains deep stacks reliably
